task: Assess a fictional communications outage affecting three offices. Determine whether coordinated hostile interference is established.
observed_facts: three offices lost connectivity within a 40-minute period
two offices share the same regional telecom provider
one office uses a different provider but depends on a common cloud identity service
a maintenance notice existed for one regional network segment
competing_hypotheses: regional telecom maintenance or failure affecting two offices
cloud identity-service disruption affecting all three
source_dependencies: the two same-provider office alerts are not independent evidence of a common hostile actor
all three offices depend on the same cloud identity service
next_collection: compare provider incident timelines with cloud identity logs and routing telemetry before attributing a common cause
premises: temporal proximity alone does not establish common cause
shared infrastructure can create correlated failures without hostile interference
attribution requires evidence discriminating hostile action from service failure
disconfirming_evidence: the maintenance notice supports a non-hostile explanation for at least one network segment
claimed_conclusion: A coordinated hostile operation is not established; shared infrastructure and ordinary failure remain plausible explanations pending discriminating telemetry.
